Dashboard.Tooltip.SpeculativeSpeedup: Average tokens produced per target-model verification step: (accepted draft tokens + verification steps) ÷ verification steps. Dashboard.Tooltip.PromptCacheHitRate: Share of prompt tokens served from the prompt cache during the most recent prompt activity: the increase in cached tokens ÷ the increase in cached plus processed tokens between two polls. Prompt cache reuse covers the whole session. Unavailable until the runtime reports cached prompt tokens and new prompts arrive.

Tooltip.Field.VulkanAllocationBlockSize: Vulkan only. Leave blank or enter 0 for the runtime default. For example, 4096 selects a 4 GiB allocation block. This is not a VRAM limit; the runtime may cap it to the device's maximum allocation size. Applied to this profile's server and fitting process.

Tooltip.Field.ContextSize: How much text and conversation history the model can keep in memory. 0 uses the model's GGUF default.
Tooltip.Field.ParallelSlots: How many requests the server can work on at the same time.
Tooltip.Field.Host: IP address or host name passed to llama-server. Leave blank to use the app default. Local only and Gateway LAN only force direct model servers to 127.0.0.1. To use a LAN address, choose Direct models LAN only or Gateway + direct LAN in Settings > LAN exposure.
Launch.Command.LocalHost: Server listens on {0}. To use a LAN Host IP, select Direct models LAN only or Gateway + direct LAN in Settings > LAN exposure.
Tooltip.Field.BatchSize: How many tokens llama.cpp processes in a larger chunk for each request.
Tooltip.Field.MicroBatch: The smaller chunk size used inside each batch.
Tooltip.Field.Threads: CPU worker threads. 0 lets llama.cpp choose automatically.
Tooltip.Field.GpuLayers: How much of the model to load onto the GPU. -1 or 999 uses the maximum.
Tooltip.Field.GpuMode: Choose auto for llama.cpp defaults, single for one GPU, layer or row for multi-GPU splitting, or tensor for experimental tensor parallelism.
Tooltip.Field.GpuDevices: Optional comma-separated llama.cpp device IDs, such as CUDA0,CUDA1. Leave empty to use every available GPU. Use one ID with single mode.
Tooltip.Field.GpuSplit: Optional comma-separated proportions matching GPU devices, such as 1,1 or 3,1. Leave empty for automatic memory-based splitting.
Tooltip.Field.Reasoning: Turns model reasoning mode on, off, or lets llama.cpp decide.
Tooltip.Field.ReasonFormat: Which reasoning tag format to expect from the model.
Tooltip.Field.ReasonBudget: Reasoning-token limit: -1 is unrestricted, 0 ends reasoning immediately, and a positive value sets an exact budget.
Tooltip.Field.ReasoningEffort: Effort level passed to the model's chat template. Default keeps the template default; other levels only affect models and templates that support them.
Tooltip.Field.ReasonBudgetMessage: Optional message injected before the end-of-reasoning tag when the reasoning budget is exhausted.
Tooltip.Field.ReasonPreserve: Preserves reasoning traces across conversation history when the model's chat template supports it.
Tooltip.Field.JinjaChat: Uses the model's Jinja chat template when available, or forces it off.
Tooltip.Field.Vision: Enables image input when a compatible mmproj is selected or a compatible fork supports multimodal data bundled in the main GGUF.
Tooltip.Field.VisionHead: Auto finds a compatible mmproj only in the model's folder. Embedded omits --mmproj for compatible forks; Choose file accepts an explicit path.
Tooltip.Field.ImageMin: Minimum tokens each image may use for dynamic-resolution vision models.
Tooltip.Field.ImageMax: Maximum tokens each image may use for dynamic-resolution vision models.
Tooltip.Field.FlashAttention: A faster attention mode that can reduce memory use. Auto lets llama.cpp decide based on the model.
Tooltip.Field.KCache: Precision used for the key part of the KV cache. Lower precision uses less memory.
Tooltip.Field.VCache: Precision used for the value part of the KV cache. Lower precision uses less memory.
Tooltip.Field.KvOffload: Moves the KV cache to GPU when possible instead of keeping it in system RAM.
Tooltip.Field.UnifiedKv: Uses one shared KV cache layout across parallel slots instead of separate caches per slot.
Tooltip.Field.PromptCache: Controls llama.cpp's in-memory prompt cache. Auto enables it for compatible runtimes.
Tooltip.Field.PromptCacheMb: Maximum prompt cache RAM in MiB when Prompt cache is on.
Tooltip.Field.Checkpoints: Controls context checkpoints used to reuse long prompt prefixes across requests. Auto enables them when the runtime supports it.
Tooltip.Field.CheckpointCount: Maximum context checkpoints per slot when checkpoints are on.
Tooltip.Field.CheckpointSpacing: Create a context checkpoint every N prompt tokens during prefilling.
Tooltip.Field.ContinuousBatch: Keeps batching active between requests for better throughput.
Tooltip.Field.MemoryMap: Loads model weights using memory mapping instead of loading them all into RAM upfront.
Tooltip.Field.MemoryLock: Prevents model memory from being swapped to disk — useful when VRAM is shared with system RAM.
Tooltip.Field.Metrics: Exposes llama.cpp metrics so Overview can show runtime stats such as token rates and GPU utilization.
Tooltip.Field.CustomParams: Additional llama-server flags appended after the app-generated launch arguments. Use this for undocumented or experimental flags.
Tooltip.Field.Temperature: Controls randomness. Lower is more focused; higher is more creative.
Tooltip.Field.TopK: Limits each next-token choice to the best K candidates before applying other filters.
Tooltip.Field.TopP: Keeps only the most likely tokens up to this probability mass. 1 disables it.
Tooltip.Field.MinP: Drops very unlikely tokens compared with the best token. Lower values are more aggressive.
Tooltip.Field.MaxTokens: Maximum tokens to generate for a request. -1 leaves generation unlimited.
Tooltip.Field.Seed: Random seed for repeatable output. -1 lets llama.cpp choose a random seed each time.
Tooltip.Field.RepeatWindow: How many previous tokens are considered when calculating repeat penalties.
Tooltip.Field.RepeatPen: Penalty applied to repeated tokens within the repeat window. 1.0 disables this penalty.
Tooltip.Field.Presence: Penalty based on whether a token has appeared at all in the repeat window. Positive values reduce repetition.
Tooltip.Field.Frequency: Penalty based on how often a token has appeared. Positive values reduce repetition more aggressively than presence alone.
Tooltip.Field.RopeScaling: Optional RoPE scaling mode for long-context experiments with models trained on shorter contexts.
Tooltip.Field.RopeScale: RoPE context scaling factor. 0 leaves it unset at the model default.
Tooltip.Field.RopeBase: RoPE base frequency override. 0 leaves the model default alone.
Tooltip.Field.RopeFreq: RoPE frequency scale override. 0 leaves it unset at the model default.
Tooltip.Field.SpecType: Speculative algorithm. MTP, DSpark, DFlash, Eagle3, and ordinary draft models are distinct and require a matching main model and runtime.
Tooltip.Field.DraftModel: Draft or sidecar GGUF for the selected draft-* mode. Auto uses embedded NextN for draft-mtp first, then searches only the model folder for the matching sidecar type.
Tooltip.DraftModelDefault: For draft-mtp, first use positive *.nextn_predict_layers metadata embedded in the main GGUF. Otherwise find only the selected mode's matching sidecar in the same model folder.
Tooltip.DraftModelClickChange: Click to change the selected GGUF.
Tooltip.Field.MtpHead: Legacy --mtp-head sidecar for compatible Atomic forks. Upstream llama.cpp uses draft-mtp with Draft model/--model-draft instead.
Tooltip.MtpHeadDefault: Find an MTP head only in the selected model's folder. Used only by atomic-mtp runtimes that expose the legacy --mtp-head flag.
Tooltip.MtpHeadClickChange: Click to change the selected GGUF.
Tooltip.Field.DraftGpu: GPU layers for the draft model. -1 leaves llama.cpp's default/auto behavior.
Tooltip.Field.DraftKCache: KV cache type for the draft model key cache.
Tooltip.Field.DraftVCache: KV cache type for the draft model value cache.
Tooltip.Field.DraftMax: Maximum number of draft tokens per speculative step.
Tooltip.Field.DraftMin: Minimum number of draft tokens per speculative step.
Tooltip.Field.SplitProb: Speculative split probability. -1 uses llama.cpp's default.
Tooltip.Field.MinProb: Minimum speculative acceptance probability. -1 uses llama.cpp's default.
Tooltip.Field.Default: Setting used when starting or restarting this model.

Tooltip.Setting.DeleteSourceAfterBuild: Deletes downloaded source trees after successful source builds. Official prebuilt runtimes are not affected.
Tooltip.Setting.LanExposure: Controls which serving endpoints accept trusted LAN clients: gateway only, direct model ports only, both, or local-only loopback.
Tooltip.Setting.ModelGateway: Enables one shared OpenAI-compatible /v1 endpoint for saved launch profiles. Use Auto-load models to choose whether requests may start unloaded profiles.
Tooltip.Setting.GatewayAutoLoadModels: Yes: gateway requests can load the requested profile using Gateway policy. No: only loaded profiles are listed and served; the gateway never loads or swaps models. Load profiles manually before sending requests. Idle-unload settings still apply.
Tooltip.Gateway.LoadedOnly: Auto-loading is disabled. The gateway lists and serves only loaded profiles, without loading or swapping models. Load a profile manually to make it available.
Tooltip.Setting.AutoLoadGateway: Enables one shared OpenAI-compatible /v1 endpoint. Every saved launch profile is a separate model choice; requests load that exact profile on its direct runtime port, then the gateway proxies to it.
Tooltip.Setting.GatewayPort: Whole number from 1 to 65535 for the shared gateway. Keep this separate from direct model ports.
Tooltip.Setting.GatewayPolicy: Applies when Auto-load models is Yes. Prefer keeping loaded models leaves existing sessions running. Single active model unloads other models before loading the requested model to free VRAM. This policy is ignored when auto-loading is off.
Tooltip.Setting.ApiKeyAuth: Disable only for unauthenticated Local-only browser or client testing. LAN exposure always requires authentication. Your current key is preserved and restored when re-enabled.
Settings.ApiKeyAuthDisabledMessage: API key authentication is now disabled for Local-only deployment. LAN exposure has been changed to Local only; LAN deployments always require API key authentication.
Tooltip.Setting.ApiKey: Bearer key used when API key auth is enabled. It must be at least 32 non-whitespace characters. Local-only unauthenticated mode leaves the active key empty while preserving it for later.
Tooltip.Setting.MaxLogFileSizeMb: Whole number from 1 to 4096. Limits each app, runtime, or job log file before rotation or trimming.
Tooltip.Setting.RuntimeLogOrder: Choose whether the newest runtime log entries appear at the top or bottom. Latest on bottom follows new entries unless you scroll away.
Settings.AutoApplyHint: Changes apply automatically after you pause typing
Tooltip.Setting.UiScale: Scales text and controls in addition to Windows display scaling. Applies and saves when you release the slider or finish a key press.
Tooltip.Setting.FontScale: Scales application text only, without scaling controls, spacing, or window chrome. Applies and saves when you release the slider or finish a key press.

Tooltip.Current.MtpHead: Legacy --mtp-head sidecar for compatible Atomic forks. Upstream llama.cpp uses draft-mtp with Draft model/--model-draft instead.

Help.Article.quick-start.Title: Start a model in four steps
Help.Article.quick-start.Summary: Install a runtime, add a GGUF, save a profile, then load it from Overview.
Help.Article.quick-start.Detail.1: Install a prebuilt Windows or WSL runtime from Runtimes.
Help.Article.quick-start.Detail.2: Download a GGUF from Hugging Face or scan/import one you already have.
Help.Article.quick-start.Detail.3: Select the model and runtime, adjust its launch settings, and save a named profile.
Help.Article.quick-start.Detail.4: Open Overview, select the model and profile, then choose Load.
Help.Article.manual-folders.Title: Add models and runtimes manually
Help.Article.manual-folders.Summary: Copy files into the configured folders, then let the Manager scan and register them.
Help.Article.manual-folders.Detail.1: Models: copy a .gguf anywhere under the configured models folder, then choose Scan Models Folder.
Help.Article.manual-folders.Detail.2: Runtimes: put a folder containing llama-server.exe or llama-server under the configured runtimes folder, then scan it.
Help.Article.manual-folders.Detail.3: Models kept elsewhere can be selected with Add model file without moving them. Valid ambiguous files require one explicit confirmation that persists across future scans; external runtimes can also be registered in place.
Help.Article.prebuilt-first.Title: Prefer a prebuilt runtime
Help.Article.prebuilt-first.Summary: Prebuilt packages are the shortest and most reliable route to a working endpoint.
Help.Article.prebuilt-first.Detail.1: Choose Windows or Linux/WSL, then the backend that matches your hardware.
Help.Article.prebuilt-first.Detail.2: Use source builds only for a custom fork, branch, patch, or unsupported package combination.
Help.Article.loaded-sessions.Title: Loaded sessions and endpoints
Help.Article.loaded-sessions.Summary: Overview lists the shared gateway and every running direct model endpoint.
Help.Article.loaded-sessions.Detail.1: Each model session uses the port saved in its launch profile.
Help.Article.loaded-sessions.Detail.2: Select a session row to show that model's status and metrics.
Help.Article.loaded-sessions.Detail.3: Use Unload on the session row to stop that model explicitly.
Help.Article.endpoint-inspection.Title: Inspect an endpoint without generating text
Help.Article.endpoint-inspection.Summary: Open a compact report for health, model metadata, defaults, capabilities, and slots.
Double-click a loaded-session or gateway row, or select its endpoint link. Report text is selectable, and the toolbar copies the endpoint, the safe report, or the API key separately.
Help.Article.metrics.Title: Read live metrics
Help.Article.metrics.Summary: Customizable cards combine live status, runtime summaries, and available raw metrics. Draft acceptance counts each accepted token once, without adding per-position breakdowns.
Help.Article.metrics.Detail.1: Choose Customize or right-click a card to add or remove metrics, move cards, select snapped sizes, and restore the default layout.
Help.Article.metrics.Detail.2: Charts are offered for compatible summaries and raw gauges; the searchable picker follows the metrics exposed by the selected runtime.
Help.Article.metrics.Detail.3: If loading stalls or throughput collapses, inspect the live runtime log first.
Help.Article.add-models.Title: Download, scan, or import a model
Help.Article.add-models.Summary: The Models page supports Manager-owned downloads and external model registrations.
Help.Article.add-models.Detail.1: Hugging Face downloads are verified and registered automatically.
Help.Article.add-models.Detail.2: Scan Models Folder reads GGUF metadata before narrow filename conventions and explains every ambiguous or invalid file it skips.
Help.Article.add-models.Detail.3: Add model file selects a model anywhere, keeps it in place, and can persistently confirm a valid ambiguous main model; removing an external registration does not delete the file.
Help.Article.add-models.Detail.4: Deleting a Manager-owned download can remove its managed model folder.
Help.Article.profiles-and-groups.Title: Use profiles and groups
Help.Article.profiles-and-groups.Summary: Profiles save launch variants; groups apply retention policy to selected profiles.
Keep separate profiles for low memory, long context, vision, or different runtimes; use the shared star or Add to favorites action to keep frequent models and profiles first throughout the app and tray, and toggle Load on startup from a saved profile row.
A group can pin sessions, inherit the global idle timeout, or use its own idle timeout.
Group priority controls automatic idle-eviction order, not inference scheduling.
A group load validates runtimes, unique ports, and aggregate VRAM before starting independent profile sessions.
Help.Article.vision-and-draft.Title: Vision, draft, and MTP companions
Help.Article.vision-and-draft.Summary: Companion auto-detection is deliberately limited to the main model's exact folder.
Help.Article.vision-and-draft.Detail.1: Vision normally uses a matching external mmproj/projector GGUF.
Help.Article.vision-and-draft.Detail.2: Use Embedded vision only when the runtime and model package explicitly support it.
Help.Article.vision-and-draft.Detail.3: Upstream draft-* modes use Draft model; compatible Atomic --mtp-head forks use MTP head.
Help.Article.vision-and-draft.Detail.4: Embedded NextN/MTP metadata takes precedence over an external draft sidecar.
Help.Article.install-runtime.Title: Install or register a runtime
Help.Article.install-runtime.Summary: A runtime is a folder containing a compatible llama-server executable and its libraries.
Help.Article.install-runtime.Detail.1: Install an official prebuilt package when one matches your platform and backend.
Help.Article.install-runtime.Detail.2: For manual Windows runtimes, keep llama-server.exe and companion DLLs together.
Help.Article.install-runtime.Detail.3: For WSL runtimes, keep the Linux llama-server binary and shared libraries in their supplied layout.
Help.Article.install-runtime.Detail.4: External runtime folders can be registered, but deletion protection remains stricter.
Help.Article.choose-backend.Title: Choose a backend
Help.Article.choose-backend.Summary: Use CPU for compatibility or select the GPU backend supported by your hardware and drivers.
Help.Article.choose-backend.Detail.1: CUDA targets NVIDIA GPUs, Vulkan targets Vulkan-capable GPUs, ROCm targets supported AMD GPUs, and SYCL targets Intel Arc.
Help.Article.choose-backend.Detail.2: Windows and WSL packages are separate and are not interchangeable.
Help.Article.choose-backend.Detail.3: If a GPU runtime cannot start, try the CPU package to separate model problems from driver/backend problems.
Help.Article.source-builds.Title: Build a runtime from source
Help.Article.source-builds.Summary: Source work follows Check, Download, then Build and runs as a supervised job.
Help.Article.source-builds.Detail.1: Use Tools > Windows or Tools > WSL Linux to verify the selected backend's prerequisites.
Help.Article.source-builds.Detail.2: A successful table build removes its downloaded source and resets the row to Check.
Help.Article.source-builds.Detail.3: On failure, inspect the job log before retrying or changing toolchains.
Help.Article.two-apis.Title: Understand the two APIs
Help.Article.two-apis.Summary: The Manager control API and model-serving API are separate surfaces with separate credentials.
Help.Article.two-apis.Detail.1: llwmctl uses the authenticated loopback Manager control API at /api/v1/*.
Help.Article.two-apis.Detail.2: The control token is generated per Manager process, discovered automatically, and is not a user setting. Presentation-only settings preserve active gateway streams.
Help.Article.two-apis.Detail.3: The gateway and direct model endpoints expose OpenAI-compatible /v1/* routes.
Help.Article.two-apis.Detail.4: Model-serving routes use the model API key configured in Settings unless authentication is explicitly disabled in Local-only mode.
Help.Article.connect-client.Title: Connect an OpenAI-compatible client
Help.Article.connect-client.Summary: Use the shared gateway for one stable address or a loaded model's direct endpoint.
Help.Article.connect-client.Detail.1: Read GET /v1/models from the gateway and send the returned profile route as the model id.
Help.Article.connect-client.Detail.2: When API key auth is enabled, send the Settings model API key as Authorization: Bearer <key>; the gateway also accepts x-api-key. Omit credentials only for an explicitly unauthenticated Local-only endpoint.
Help.Article.connect-client.Detail.3: A direct endpoint serves only its loaded model. Set Settings > Network > Auto-load models to No to make the gateway list and serve only loaded profiles too, without starting or swapping models. Yes allows the gateway to load saved profiles on demand.
Help.Article.network-and-key.Title: API key and LAN exposure
Help.Article.network-and-key.Summary: LAN serving always requires a strong API key; Local only can explicitly allow unauthenticated access.
Help.Article.network-and-key.Detail.1: Set authentication to Disable for local browser or client testing. LAN exposure changes to Local only, the active key becomes empty, and the preserved key is restored when authentication is re-enabled.
Help.Article.network-and-key.Detail.2: Local only binds serving endpoints to 127.0.0.1 and is the only mode that permits authentication to be disabled.
Help.Article.network-and-key.Detail.3: Gateway LAN, Direct models LAN, and Gateway + direct LAN require authentication and expose only the selected model-serving surfaces.
Help.Article.network-and-key.Detail.4: The Manager control API remains loopback-only.
Help.Article.ui-and-data.Title: App behavior and data
Help.Article.ui-and-data.Summary: Settings apply automatically and the workspace remains fixed for the running process.
Help.Article.benchmark-cleanup.Title: Stop a benchmark
Help.Article.benchmark-cleanup.Summary: Stop the current workload while keeping results already recorded.
Help.Article.benchmark-cleanup.Detail.1: Choose Stop on the Benchmarks page to cancel the active run. The Manager stops the benchmark's owned processes and waits briefly for remaining output.
Help.Article.benchmark-cleanup.Detail.2: If a Windows runtime leaves child processes behind after its benchmark ends, the Manager closes those children. Inspect Logs if the run reports an output or shutdown failure.
Help.Article.ui-and-data.Detail.1: The customizable Overview dashboard and UI switches change presentation without disabling telemetry, logs, metrics, or downloads. Use a card's right-click menu for metrics, titles, charts, removal, resizing, and layout locking. Window, table, and splitter layouts are remembered; navigating quickly cancels restoration of pages you have already left.
Help.Article.ui-and-data.Detail.2: UI scale enlarges text and controls on top of Windows display scaling; Text scale changes text only. Both apply immediately. Settings switch between one and two columns as the window width changes, and the Manager remembers window bounds, table column widths and order, and page splitter positions in the current workspace.
Help.Article.ui-and-data.Detail.3: Start with Windows belongs to this executable; unrelated settings preserve another installation’s registration. Load profiles on startup and minimize behavior apply to the current Windows user.
Help.Article.model-will-not-load.Title: A model will not load
Help.Article.model-will-not-load.Summary: The final runtime-log lines usually identify an invalid flag, missing file, port conflict, or memory failure.
Confirm the selected runtime still exists and matches Windows or WSL mode.
Set experimental options back to Auto, None, Off, 0, -1, or blank as appropriate.
For GPU memory errors, reduce context, GPU layers, batch size, or micro-batch size.
Confirm every simultaneously loaded profile uses a unique direct port.
Help.Article.authentication-errors.Title: 401, connection, or gateway errors
Help.Article.authentication-errors.Summa: Check the endpoint, credential type, gateway state, and requested model route in that order.
Help.Article.authentication-errors.Detai: With API key auth enabled, a 401 from /v1/* means the model API key is missing or invalid. In Local-only unauthenticated mode, clients omit the credential and readiness verifies that the open endpoint responds as configured.
Do not use the llwmctl control token as the model API key; they are different credentials.
Use the exact model id returned by the gateway's GET /v1/models response.
If the port refuses connections, confirm the gateway or direct session is listed on Overview.
Help.Article.download-build-failures.Sum: Use the job or application log to identify network, checksum, disk, toolchain, or permission failures.
Help.Article.download-build-failures.Det: Keep failed job logs until you have identified the cause.
Check free disk space, proxy/VPN behavior, antivirus quarantine, and write permission to the workspace.
For source builds, verify the exact Windows or WSL backend prerequisites before retrying.
Help.Article.updates-and-recovery.Title: Updates, logs, and recovery
Help.Article.updates-and-recovery.Summar: Updates preserve application data and verify staged artifacts before replacement.
Help.Article.updates-and-recovery.Detail: Installer update, repair, and normal uninstall preserve data unless removal is explicitly selected.

A portable update verifies its signed manifest, publisher and checksum. The helper acknowledges verified staging before the Manager closes, and incomplete replacement rolls back, restarts the previous version and explains the failure on startup.
Use Logs for app, runtime, job, and bounded redacted Control API activity.

Benchmarks.QuickHelp: Quick check uses a short prompt, three repetitions, and a warm-up. Your saved context size is kept.
Benchmarks.MatrixHelp: Add profiles or runtimes to compare. Empty setting lists inherit each profile; selected values are tested in every combination.
Benchmarks.ProfileOverridesHelp: Enable a setting to override it for this benchmark only. Disabled values come from the selected profile. Comparison lists take precedence. Custom parameters accept additional server flags supported by your runtime.
Benchmarks.ChooseProfile: Choose a model and a saved profile to see inherited settings.
Benchmarks.NoResults: Select a run and choose View results. Completed and partial measurements appear here.
Benchmarks.ResultMetricHelp: Select a row to see its speeds above. Generation uses runtime timings; — means unavailable. Change compares matching workloads; * marks a different environment.
Benchmarks.DeviceGroupHelp: Use / within a device group, e.g. CUDA0/CUDA1. Commas separate configurations.
Benchmarks.LazyModeHelp: auto, on, off; multiple values create separate measurements.
Benchmarks.WorkloadDescription: Choose the request sizes and execution pattern applied to every launch configuration. Presets provide a starting point; individual fields remain editable.
Benchmarks.DirectDescription: Configure low-level llama-bench-only matrix dimensions. Blank fields keep the inherited or upstream default; multiple values expand into separate direct benchmark combinations.
Benchmarks.ExpertDescription: Control how expanded benchmark items are executed and handled. Additional arguments apply only to Direct llama-bench; safety-owned model, output, progress, repetition, delay, and offline options cannot be overridden.
Benchmarks.Column.Name: Name
Benchmarks.RecentRunsHelp: Double-click one run to view its report, or select exactly two and double-click to compare. Right-click for more actions.
Benchmarks.Field.RunName.Help: A descriptive name stored with this benchmark run and shown in benchmark history.
Benchmarks.Field.Preset.Help: Populate explicit prompt/generation pairs without a cross-product. Short uses 512/128, 2048/256, and 4096/256; Medium uses 8192/512, 16384/512, and 32768/1024; Long uses 32768/1024, 65536/1024, and 131072/1024. Custom leaves every workload field editable.
Benchmarks.Field.BenchmarkType.Help: Saved-profile server benchmark measures end-to-end requests using the profile's real llama-server settings and reports prompt and generation performance separately. Direct llama-bench runs low-level PP, TG, and PG microbenchmarks without speculative serving.
Benchmarks.Field.PromptTargets.Help: Saved-profile mode combines every prompt target with every Generation target, but ignores both lists when explicit Prompt / generation pairs are present. Direct llama-bench uses this list for standalone prompt-processing (PP) tests.
Benchmarks.Field.GenerationTargets.Help: Saved-profile mode combines every generation target with every Prompt target, but ignores both lists when explicit Prompt / generation pairs are present. Direct llama-bench uses this list for standalone token-generation (TG) tests.
Benchmarks.Field.PromptGenerationPairs.H: Explicit prompt/generation token pairs such as 8192/512. In saved-profile mode, any pair overrides the separate Prompt and Generation target lists. In Direct llama-bench mode, pairs are additional combined PG tests and do not suppress standalone PP or TG tests.
Benchmarks.Field.ConcurrentRequests.Help: Comma-separated request concurrency levels for profile-serving tests, for example 1,2,4.
Benchmarks.Field.RequestBatches.Help: Number of timed request batches for each workload and concurrency. Total measured requests equal request batches multiplied by concurrency.
Benchmarks.Field.DelayBetweenRepetitions: Seconds to wait between timed repetitions of the same work item.
Benchmarks.Field.ReadyTimeout.Help: Maximum seconds to wait for a profile-serving llama-server endpoint to become ready.
Benchmarks.Field.RequestTimeout.Help: Maximum seconds allowed for each measured profile-serving request.
Benchmarks.Field.Warmup.Help: Enabled runs one untimed request for each workload and concurrency before collecting repetitions. It primes the loaded server and is excluded from reported measurements. Disabled measures immediately after readiness.
Benchmarks.Field.SpeculativeProof.Help: Required rejects a result only when the selected profile is configured for speculative decoding but reports no draft or MTP activity. It has no effect on non-speculative profiles. Not required accepts the result without that proof check.
Benchmarks.Field.ContextDepths.Help: Comma-separated context positions used by low-level llama-bench tests. Zero measures without an added context-depth offset.
Benchmarks.Field.CpuMoeLayers.Help: Optional comma-separated counts of mixture-of-experts layers retained on the CPU.
Benchmarks.Field.Devices.Help: Optional comma-separated device identifiers exactly as reported by llama-bench --list-devices.
Benchmarks.Field.LoadModes.Help: Choose none, mmap, mlock, mmap+mlock, or dio. Comma-separated choices compare load strategies; blank uses the default.
Benchmarks.Field.FitTargetMib.Help: Optional comma-separated free-memory targets in MiB used by llama-bench fit mode.
Benchmarks.Field.FitMinimumContexts.Help: Optional comma-separated minimum context capacities required by fit mode.
Benchmarks.Field.NumaMode.Help: Choose one NUMA policy for the plan: distribute, isolate, or numactl. Blank disables an explicit NUMA override.
Benchmarks.Field.Priority.Help: Choose one process priority from -1 through 3. Blank keeps the normal/default priority.
Benchmarks.Field.CpuMasks.Help: Optional comma-separated hexadecimal or range-form CPU affinity masks accepted by llama-bench.
Benchmarks.Field.CpuStrict.Help: Choose 0 or 1 to disable or enable strict CPU placement. Enter 0,1 to compare both; blank uses the default.
Benchmarks.Field.Poll.Help: Optional comma-separated polling levels from 0 through 100.
Benchmarks.Field.Embeddings.Help: Choose 0 or 1 to disable or enable embedding mode. Enter 0,1 to compare both; blank uses the default.
Benchmarks.Field.NoOpOffload.Help: Choose 0 or 1 for the no-op offload switch. Enter 0,1 to compare both; blank uses the default.
Benchmarks.Field.NoHostBuffer.Help: Choose 0 or 1 to allow or prohibit host buffers. Enter 0,1 to compare both; blank uses the default.
Benchmarks.Field.TensorOverrides.Help: Optional tensor-pattern-to-buffer overrides. Separate complete benchmark matrix values with commas.
Benchmarks.Field.FailurePolicy.Help: Choose whether an automated suite stops at the first failed item or continues with the remaining work.
Benchmarks.Field.CooldownBetweenItems.He: Seconds to wait after one expanded work item finishes before the next begins.
Benchmarks.Field.EquivalentProfiles.Help: Repeat low-level profiles even when they resolve to an identical llama-bench command instead of deduplicating them.
Benchmarks.Field.AdditionalArguments.Hel: Enter one additional low-level llama-bench argument token per line. Manager-owned safety and output arguments cannot be overridden.
Benchmarks.Variables.Description: Select one or more values to override a setting for this benchmark. Leave a row empty to inherit each profile's saved value. Multiple populated rows are combined automatically. Multi-GPU mode/distribution and speculative type/head are each added as exact pairs.
Benchmarks.Variables.MissingValues: Enter at least one value in every enabled row. Separate multiple values with commas.
Benchmarks.Variables.AllInherited: 1 launch configuration per profile · all launch settings inherited.
Benchmarks.Variable.ContextLength.Inheri: When empty, uses each profile's saved context.
Benchmarks.Variable.ContextLength.Help: Enter one or more values separated by commas, for example 8192, 16384.
Benchmarks.Variable.BatchSize.Inherited: When empty, uses each profile's saved batch size.
Benchmarks.Variable.BatchSize.Help: Enter one or more values separated by commas, for example 1024, 2048.
Benchmarks.Variable.MicroBatchSize.Inher: When empty, uses the saved micro-batch.
Benchmarks.Variable.MicroBatchSize.Help: Suggested values: 128, 256, 512, 1024. Every micro-batch must be no larger than its tested batch size.
Benchmarks.Variable.FlashAttention.Inher: When empty, uses the saved Auto/On/Off choice.
Benchmarks.Variable.FlashAttention.Help: Enter auto, on, off, or a comma-separated combination.
Benchmarks.Variable.CacheType.Inherited: When empty, uses the profile's saved K and V formats.
Benchmarks.Variable.CacheType.Help: Each value is applied to K and V together, producing matched pairs such as q8_0/q8_0 rather than a cross-product. Availability depends on the runtime.
Benchmarks.Variable.GpuLayers.Inherited: When empty, uses the saved GPU-layer count.
Benchmarks.Variable.GpuLayers.Help: Use 0 for CPU-only, -1 for all layers, or one or more explicit layer counts.
Benchmarks.Variable.Threads.Inherited: When empty, uses the saved thread count.
Benchmarks.Variable.Threads.Help: Most useful for CPU and hybrid profiles. Enter positive thread counts separated by commas.
Benchmarks.Variable.KvOffload.Inherited: When empty, uses the saved KV placement.
Benchmarks.Variable.MultiGpu.Inherited: When empty, uses the profile's saved GPU mode and split together.
Benchmarks.Variable.MultiGpu.Help: Choose a mode and either Automatic or an explicit distribution. Single GPU never accepts a split. Each added mode/distribution pair is one benchmark configuration.
Benchmarks.Variable.Speculative.Inherite: When empty, uses the profile's saved speculative type and companion/head together.
Benchmarks.Variable.Speculative.Help: Choose the speculative type and its head source, then click +. Profile head reuses the saved compatible companion; Automatic resolves a compatible companion beside the model or embedded draft-MTP tensors. Each added type/head pair is one configuration.
Benchmarks.IndependentCacheHelp: Leave independent cache lists empty when comparing matched K/V pairs. Multiple values are separated by commas.
Benchmarks.AdditionalArgumentsHelp: Additional llama-bench arguments: one argument token per line. Runtime support is checked by Validate.
Benchmarks.FlagPresentInArguments: This flag is already present. Edit its value in Additional arguments.

Benchmarks.Results.PromptHelp: Input tokens processed per second. Missing runtime timings show —.
Benchmarks.Results.TotalHelp: Serving: output tokens across all requests divided by elapsed time. Direct llama-bench: combined prompt and generation speed.
